newsitem.title: UK: Germany to sell at least 75,000 bpd of oil - trade.
newsitem.headline: Germany to sell at least 75,000 bpd of oil - trade.

text.p: A German government plan to raise around 400 million marks ($230 million) from sales of strategic oil stocks will release at least 75,000 barrels per day on to the market for the remainder of the year, industry sources said.

Senior oil traders said the crude oil earmarked for the sale -- stored in salt caverns near the northern port of Wilhelmshaven -- would include cheaper Middle Eastern and Russian sour crudes along with more pricey low-sulphur crudes.

World benchmark Brent blend crude oil for August delivery was trading at $17.96 a barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Thursday but sources said the German government would have to bank on achieving a lower price for its oil.
"I wouldn't calculate that they will get $18 a barrel for the oil," said a trader at a leading German refiner.
"That would mean all the oil would be low-sulphur crude and that is certainly not the case," he said.

Analysts said the sale would depress oil markets which are already feeling the strain of rising industry stocks, slackening U.S. demand for gasoline and the prospect of a resumption of Iraqi exports under a U.N. oil-for-food plan.
"The timing is immaculate but if the German government believes prices are going lower then it makes sense for them," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at Swiss bank UBS.
